_provenance.what: The reference Kālasetu is fitted and verified against (see the header of source/tools/kalasetu-reference.mjs).
_provenance.sun_and_planets: JPL DE422 (Folkner 2009) over JD 625648.5–2816816.5 (about 3000 BCE – 3000 CE); outside it, a numerical integration (source/tools/nbody.mjs: Sun, Moon and nine planets as point masses with DE422's masses and the Sun's post-Newtonian term, Yoshida sixth order, step 0.125 day) started from DE422's own states at its span's edges.
_provenance.moon_and_true_node: DE422 over its span; outside it astronomy-engine, the site's modern engine — not independent before 3000 BCE.
_provenance.mean_node: the published polynomial engine.js meanNodeModern() uses
_provenance.frame: apparent geocentric, true ecliptic of date (astronomy-engine's rotation), less engine.js's Samanvaya–Ecliptic ayanāṃśa; civil time to TT with deltat.js

integrator_check.note: heliocentric direction, arcseconds, integration minus DE422 after starting from DE422 at 3000 BCE

moon_correction.note: arcseconds; T in Julian centuries from J2000; residual rms is the scatter left on the overlap

modern_vs_reference.note: the modern engine (astronomy-engine) minus this reference, arcminutes, on the verification draw
